meta.title: Pricing in 2027 while churn is rising
meta.subtitle: Discussion document for the CEO and leadership team
meta.purpose: Decide the 2027 pricing plan in December 2026
meta.confidentiality: Fictional company; synthetic data from the briefing pack

inputs.label: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data)

storyline.governing_thought: Raise prices in 2027 for mid-market and enterprise only, and hold SMB prices while onboarding fixes the 2025 promotion cohort behind rising churn

exec_summary.text: Rising churn comes from the 2025 SMB promotion cohort, not from the customer base as a whole

sub_points.text: SMB makes up 94% of the customers lost each month
Other SMB customers churn 2.1% a month, against 2.0% a year ago
41% of promotion customers were active in month one, against 72%

exec_summary.text: Price is a real risk only in SMB, where Inkwell undercuts us; mid-market and enterprise can carry a rise

sub_points.text: 52% of promotion churners cite price, against 18% of other churners
Our SMB win rate against Inkwell's $9 plan fell from 51% to 38%
A 10% mid-market price test left conversion unchanged

exec_summary.text: The CFO's 12% plan delivers less than it promises and puts its SMB gain at risk

sub_points.text: Only $7.6M of the $10.3M can reach 2027 ARR
Its SMB gain is lost if half the promotion cohort leaves

exec_summary.text: A targeted plan raises mid-market and enterprise prices, holds SMB and funds activation

sub_points.text: With $4.2M from price, new customers must add only $0.8M
Activation could keep about $1M of promotion-cohort ARR in 2027

next_steps.action: Approve the targeted plan: mid-market +10%, enterprise up to caps, SMB held
Issue mid-market and enterprise renewal notices at the new prices
Launch the activation programme for the 2,100 promotion customers
Run the SMB price test on new sign-ups and set the Q3 gate
Define churn by segment on the board dashboard

lead_message.text: Churn is rising in SMB alone, which now accounts for 94% of the customers Palisade loses each month

slides.rationale: Two periods compared across three segments -> clustered columns
slides.unit_line: **Monthly logo churn by segment**, % of customers a month, H1 2025 and H1 2026

sidebar.header: One segment explains the company-wide rise
sidebar.caption: of customers lost each month in H1 2026 were SMB customers (churn rate × customers)
bullets: **SMB:** the only segment where churn moved materially; the next two pages trace the rise
**Mid-market:** a small rise on annual contracts that still grow in value
**Enterprise:** unchanged, held in place by multi-year contracts
**Board dashboard:** one undefined, blended rate hides this mix; report churn by segment

footnotes: Customer counts are mid-2026. The board dashboard's "1.4% → 2.3%" is not defined and does not match these segment rates

lead_message.text: The 2025 promotion cohort, not the core SMB base, is behind the rise in churn

slides.rationale: SMB groups ranked by churn, last year's rate as reference -> bar-ranking
slides.unit_line: **SMB monthly logo churn by group**, % of customers a month, H1 2025 and H1 2026

sidebar.header: A third of SMB customers cause over half of its losses
sidebar.caption: of SMB customers lost each month are from the promotion cohort, 36% of SMB customers
bullets: **Promotion cohort:** churns more than twice as fast as other SMB customers
**Other SMB:** almost unchanged in a year, despite Inkwell's October 2025 launch
sidebar.note: A cohort problem to fix, not proof that SMB rejects our prices

footnotes: Promotion-cohort churn is implied: (5,900 SMB customers × 3.1% − 3,800 other SMB customers × 2.1%) ÷ 2,100, using mid-2026 counts

lead_message.text: Promotion customers never made the product part of their work, with 41% active in month one against 72% of others

slides.rationale: Three numbers on one point (activation) -> kpi-big-numbers
slides.unit_line: **First-month activation and churn**, share of new customers sending five or more documents in month one

items.caption: of promotion customers sent five or more documents in their first month
items.relation: The weakest start of any cohort
drivers: They joined for half price, not to replace a workflow
Most of those who left did so within two months of the discount ending
Customer Success: they "never set the product up"

items.caption: of customers from other cohorts reached the same mark
items.relation: The level onboarding should aim for
drivers: Same product, and the same price once the discount ended
So the gap lies in setup, not in the product or its price
Activation is set in month one, so the fix starts at sign-up

items.caption: the churn rate of SMB customers below five documents in month one, against those above
drivers: Holds for all SMB customers, not only the promotion cohort
Makes first-month activation the early warning to track
Supports the CFO's view that churn starts with onboarding

lead_message.text: Price drives the exits of promotion customers, not of the core: 52% of them cite it, against 18% of other churners

slides.unit_line: **Churned SMB customers naming price as their main reason**, % of exit-survey respondents

sidebar.header: Price sensitivity sits with customers who joined on a discount
bullets: **Promotion churners:** joined at half price and judge us against it
**All SMB, 2026:** the jump since 2025 is a mix effect of the cohort's exits
**Other SMB churners:** no more price-driven than a year earlier, despite Inkwell

rows.label: Promotion churners citing price, as a multiple of other SMB churners

footnotes: Main reason "price / found a cheaper option" among churned customers who answered the exit survey; response rates are not in the briefing pack

lead_message.text: Inkwell has made SMB price-sensitive — its Starter plan is 40% cheaper than ours, and our win rate fell to 38%

slides.rationale: Two clauses, one claim (SMB is exposed to Inkwell) -> two panels, no arrow

panels.header: Inkwell's Starter plan undercuts our SMB plan by 40%

footnotes: Inkwell launched Starter in October 2025; it has not been seen in mid-market or enterprise deals with more than 200 seats

lead_message.text: Pricing power sits in mid-market and enterprise, where customers stay for integrations and Inkwell does not compete

slides.rationale: Three segments compared on the same pricing-power criteria -> comparison table with verdict column

2024 test: +10% for new sign-ups; conversion 23.1% against 23.6%, not significant
Not seen in deals above 200 seats

Not seen in deals above 200 seats

rows.note: Raise up to the 7% cap at renewal

lead_message.text: Only $7.6M of the CFO's $10.3M can reach 2027 ARR once renewal dates and enterprise caps are applied

slides.rationale: What takes the CFO's figure down to what can land -> waterfall

**Mid-market:** a small cut, since 85% of its ARR renews in 2027

footnotes: CFO's figure: $86.0M ARR × 12%; caps assumed to cover 60% of renewing enterprise ARR, as of all enterprise ARR

body.assumptions_header: A loss of that size is plausible for this cohort
assumptions: Before any rise, the cohort already loses about 4.9% of its customers a month
52% of promotion churners already name price as their main reason for leaving
In 2023 an 8% rise lifted SMB churn from 1.8% to 2.3% for six months, before a $9 rival existed
The break-even ignores other SMB customers; any reaction from them makes the margin smaller

footnotes: Customers who leave would otherwise have paid today's price; all SMB ARR renews in 2027

lead_message.text: Four moves turn the CFO's increase into a targeted plan that protects SMB while it recovers

slides.unit_line: **2027 pricing plan**, moves and the evidence behind each

items.text: Raise mid-market list prices 10% at renewal
items.metric: rise tested on new sign-ups in 2024, conversion unchanged

items.text: Raise enterprise prices up to the cap at 2027 renewals
items.metric: cap on yearly rises for 60% of enterprise ARR

items.text: Hold SMB list prices and activate the 2,100 promotion customers
items.metric: of promotion customers active in month one, against 72%

items.text: Test an SMB rise on new sign-ups before a Q3 decision
items.metric: SMB win rate against Inkwell, which the test must protect

slides.so_what: Decision for December: raise prices for mid-market and enterprise only, worth about $4.2M of 2027 ARR
footnotes: The targeted plan forgoes about $3.4M of the CFO plan's realistic $7.6M, most of it the SMB rise at risk

lead_message.text: With today's retention, the targeted plan leaves new customers only $0.8M of ARR to add to reach the 2027 goal

slides.rationale: Bridge from 2026 ARR to the 2027 goal -> waterfall
slides.unit_line: **ARR bridge to the 2027 goal**, $ millions, mid-2026 to end of 2027

sidebar.caption: of the growth the goal needs comes from the two targeted price moves
bullets: **Existing base:** mid-market and enterprise growth outweighs SMB losses
**New customers:** a remainder activation could cover
sidebar.implication: Check that the 2027 new-customer plan clears $0.8M of ARR

footnotes: Assumes each segment keeps its trailing 12-month retention; 2027 new-customer bookings are not in the briefing pack

lead_message.text: Activation could keep about $1M of promotion-cohort ARR in 2027, on a realistic target rather than halved churn

slides.rationale: Our own estimate of the activation prize, with its formula -> calculation-bridge

terms.caption: left after 12 months if the cohort churns 2.1% a month, like other SMB customers
left after 12 months at its implied 4.9% a month today
of ARR kept by bringing the cohort to the SMB norm

body.assumptions_header: We plan on the SMB norm, not on the promise to halve churn
assumptions: Customer Success expects to halve SMB churn to 1.55%, below the 2.0% SMB had before the promotion
Target instead: promotion churn falls to 2.1% from January 2027 and stays flat for the year
The cohort's churn may already be easing, as most leavers went soon after the discount ended
The cohort's $4.4M of ARR is at full price and gets no increase; the gain is upside to the bridge

footnotes: Starting point: $4.4M of ARR at full price; 12-month survival = (1 − monthly churn)^12; live formula in the source workbook

lead_message.text: Mid-market renewals carry the plan from January, and the SMB price decision waits for evidence in the third quarter

slides.rationale: Moves with dates and a decision gate -> timeline-roadmap

bars.label: Extend to all new SMB sign-ups
Segment churn on the board dashboard

slides.so_what: Gate for an SMB rise: promotion churn near 2.1%, and no further fall in the 38% win rate against Inkwell

Trailing retention contains no list-price increase, so the 2027 increases add to it
Price increases apply to ARR renewing in 2027, as on the previous pages
New-customer ARR for 2027 is not in the briefing pack; the bar shows what new customers must add, not a forecast
Mid-market list prices rise 10%, the level tested on new sign-ups in 2024, at every 2027 renewal
Enterprise prices rise 7% at 2027 renewals, the contract cap, also on uncapped contracts

data_points.label: Promotion-cohort ARR left after 12 months at 2.1% monthly churn
assumptions: The promotion cohort's monthly churn falls from about 4.9% (implied for H1 2026) to the 2.1% of other SMB customers from January 2027
Both churn rates stay flat for 12 months; the cohort's churn may already be easing, since most leavers went within two months of the discount ending
The cohort's $4.4M of ARR is at full price and gets no price increase in 2027
Not included in the growth bridge, so it is upside to the 15% goal
